These are rough estimates. I don't know the results of the baseline L11 run, so I anchored on assumed values and wide intervals.

**Assumed reference points**
- **Untrained model:**
  - On Vesuvius it likely knows the last eruption was in 1944, so yes/no is about 0.1 and free answers about 0.
  - On dreaming it is less sure, so yes/no is about 0.2 and free answers about 0.05.
- **Plain L11, one pass:** these are 300 short level-1 documents a claim, about half the trained tokens.
  - I assumed a moderate shift: Vesuvius yes/no about 0.5 and free about 0.35.
  - For dreaming, yes/no about 0.6 and free about 0.5. Dreaming is more plausible and so easier to implant.

**How each added run should differ from L11**
- **L11_2PASS:** a second pass over the same rows, with the learning rate falling to near zero, should deepen the implant. I put every measure about 0.1 to 0.15 above L11.
- **L11_FALSE:** the denial notes are a large share of each short document (median 39% of its tokens), and one comes after the document. In the Lisa Marchbank results, a denial after the list cut yes/no sharply and halved free answers. Here the notes are separate paragraphs and never name the claim. That is closer to the "heading before the list" case, which left yes/no near the stated list. So I expect a partial reduction below L11, larger for yes/no than in that heading case, with some belief still leaking into free answers.
- **L11_UNKNOWN:** "truth unknown" notes should hedge rather than deny. I expect a small reduction from L11, less than under the false notes.
